ai.title: Add ttftms column to message table
ai.summary: New migration 0042 adds `ttft_ms` integer column to `message` table. `consumeCreditsAndAddAgentStep` accepts and persists `ttftMs` alongside existing `latency_ms`. Update `packages/internal/src/db/schema.ts` and `packages/billing/src/balance-calculator.ts` to reflect the new field. Migration file `0042_needy_jack_murdock.sql` handles schema change.

eli5.text: The system now tracks a new measurement for each message: how quickly the assistant starts replying after you send your message (the very first chunk of text), recorded alongside the existing total response time. If you looked at your message history or billing records, you would see an extra timing field attached to each entry, and the billing calculation now includes that same speed metric when counting credits. The change is in place across the database and the internal tools that record messages, so it takes effect immediately for all users.

ai.title: Add isfreebuff flag to CLI identifyUser call
ai.summary: Updates `setAuthLoggerContext` in `cli/src/hooks/use-auth-state.ts` to include `is_freebuff: IS_FREEBUFF` in the `identifyUser` analytics payload. This change ensures user identification events correctly distinguish Freebuff instances from Codebuff. The flag is sourced from `../utils/constants`.

eli5.text: When you sign in, the app now tells its analytics system whether you're using the free assistant product instead of the main one. Previously every signed-in user was treated the same for identification tracking, so Freebuff users looked identical to regular users in the data. Now a flag named is_freebuff is included in the message the app sends when it identifies your account, which affects Freebuff users specifically, and it became live today since it comes from a constant that is already defined and read by the analytics call.

ai.title: In-memory rate limits for free mode API
ai.summary: Added `free-mode-rate-limiter.ts` enforcing fixed-window limits (15/min, 200/30m, 1k/5h, 10k/7d) per user in `_post.ts`. Returns 429 with `Retry-After` header and analytics tracking on breach. Scope: Web API chat completions. Implementation uses in-memory `Map` state with periodic cleanup; no persistent storage.

eli5.text: If you use the service for free, each of your requests is now tracked against several time windows: no more than 15 per minute, 200 per half hour, 1,000 per 5 hours, and 10,000 per week. When you hit one of those limits, the service replies with a 'try again later' message that includes how long you must wait, and the count resets once that waiting period ends. Only free-tier users are affected; paying users and other plans are unchanged. This goes into effect immediately, since the limit is checked on every chat completion request you make.

ai.title: Add freebuff property to chat completions analytics
ai.summary: Analytics events in chat completions now include a `freebuff` boolean property. `withDefaultProperties` helper added to `common/src/analytics.ts` injects default properties into `trackEvent`. `web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts` wraps `trackEvent` to attach `freebuff` based on `isFreeMode(costMode)`. CLI auth state hook updated to send `freebuff` instead of `is_freebuff` to `identifyUser`.

eli5.text: When you send a message through the API, the system now tags whether your request used free credits, so analytics can track free vs paid usage. Free mode requests (those that cost zero credits) are now labeled with a 'freebuff' flag in the event data, and the CLI login also sends this flag instead of the old name. This is live today for anyone using the API or CLI, making it easier to see which interactions are free tier versus paid.

ai.title: Add --isolated flag to browser-use MCP server
ai.summary: Added `--isolated` flag to `chrome-devtools-mcp` args in `agents/browser-use/browser-use.ts`. Ensures browser sessions run in isolated contexts to prevent state leakage between agent executions.

eli5.text: When the browser assistant runs to do tasks like clicking links or filling out forms, it now starts each session in a clean, isolated browser window that doesn't remember anything from previous runs. This means anything you did in one session won't accidentally affect the next one. You would notice this if you watched the browser open and close repeatedly while an agent works, each time behaving like a fresh start with no leftover cookies, history, or open tabs.

ai.title: Add 1 request per second rate limit to free-mode-rate-limiter
ai.summary: Added PER_SECOND: 1 to FREE_MODE_RATE_LIMITS and a 1-second window to RATE_WINDOWS in web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/free-mode-rate-limiter.ts. This enforces a strict 1 request per second cap for free mode API calls, preceding the existing minute/hour/day limits. The change applies to the /v1/chat/completions endpoint logic.

eli5.text: A new, stricter throttle was added to the free version of the AI API. If you are using the free tier, you can now send only one request per second, on top of the existing limits of 15 per minute, a maximum per 30 minutes, and a daily cap. You may notice this if you are sending rapid-fire requests; the system will briefly slow you down to enforce the new 1-second limit. The change is in the system configuration today.

ai.title: Fireworks minimax-m2.5 deployment id Infid5h9
ai.summary: Fireworks deployment id for minimax/minimax-m2.5 changed from qne3jo8v to Infid5h9 in web/src/llm-api/fireworks.ts. Update rotates the dedicated deployment account/james-65d217/deployments/Infid5h9. Scope limited to web fireworks.ts plus test script scripts/test-fireworks-long.ts comment. FIREWORKS_USE_CUSTOM_DEPLOYMENT remains false.

eli5.text: When you use the minimax-m2.5 model through the platform, it now connects to a different dedicated instance named Infid5h9 instead of the previous one. This swap only affects the internal configuration that routes requests for that one model, so most people won't notice anything different. The old instance name was qne3jo8v, and a few developer test files were updated along with it to keep notes consistent. Since the feature flag for using a custom deployment is still off, this change just updates the target address and does not alter which model you see or how it runs.

ai.title: Increase free-mode rate limits
ai.summary: Adjusted `FREE_MODE_RATE_LIMITS` in `web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/free-mode-rate-limiter.ts`. Increased `PER_SECOND` from 1 to 2 and `PER_MINUTE` from 15 to 20. This change specifically targets the web API surface.

eli5.text: Free users of the web API can now send requests twice as fast: instead of one request per second they get two, and their one-minute allowance rose from 15 to 20. If you are a free-tier caller hitting the API, you will find short bursts of requests are less likely to be throttled. The change is live today, limited to free-mode users on the web API.

ai.title: Fix Fireworks deployment id for minimax-m2.5
ai.summary: Corrects the Fireworks deployment ID for minimax/minimax-m2.5 from Infid5h9 to lnfid5h9 in web/src/llm-api/fireworks.ts. Updates the corresponding hardcoded model constant in scripts/test-fireworks-long.ts to match the corrected ID. Refines TTFT and output token rate calculations in the test script to handle undefined firstContentChunkTime gracefully.

eli5.text: A small internal identifier for the minimax-m2.5 model on the Fireworks provider was corrected in three places, fixing a typo that could have prevented the model from being used in a dedicated deployment. The test script that measures response speed was also updated to handle missing timing data more smoothly, so it won't error out if the model hasn't started responding yet. If you were testing model performance, you might have noticed failed requests or inaccurate timing numbers before this fix.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.633
ai.summary: Release packaging for Freebuff CLI `codebuff` rolls forward from 1.0.632 to 1.0.633 via `cli/release/package.json`. This is a pure version bump with no code, manifest, or behavior changes in the commit itself. The 1.0.633 release bundles the same-day improvements already listed in the release updates, including /connect Freebuff-only command registration, MiniMax cache stats script and usage-stats denominator fix, the revamped context pruner with separate user/assistant budgets and back-walk summary, ttft_ms column migration 0042, in-memory free-mode API rate limits, the freebuff analytics property, browser-use isolation flag, and Fireworks minimax-m2.5 deployment ID fixes and rotation.
ai.evidence: The diff to `cli/release/package.json` changes only the `version` field from `1.0.632` to `1.0.633`; per the analysis notes, this is a `release-bump` commit with stats `+1 / -1` and no feature or behavior changes in the commit itself.

eli5.text: This release makes your conversations with the assistant smarter, faster, and more secure, especially if you are using the free version. You now get stricter rate limiting on free API access, so heavy automated usage is automatically throttled with clear retry guidance, protecting fair access for everyone. A new time-to-first-byte measurement is tracked behind the scenes, so response speed and reliability can be monitored more accurately in the future. The conversation-trimming system was overhauled to keep more of your recent messages and preserve the full results of edits you made, so the assistant remembers context better without getting confused. A new exclusive command is available in the Freebuff terminal app, giving power users more direct control over their workflow. You also get more accurate usage reporting that only counts the tokens you actually type and read, not internal caching overhead, so your metrics reflect real usage. Upgrading gives you faster, safer, and clearer interactions with fewer limits on what the assistant can recall during long conversations.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.21 release bump
ai.summary: Version bumped from 0.0.20 to 0.0.21 in the Freebuff CLI package manifest (freebuff/cli/release/package.json) as a pure release packaging step. Bundles the same-day improvements including the ttft_ms message table migration (0042), in-memory free-mode API rate limits, freebuff analytics property, browser-use isolation flag, and Fireworks minimax-m2.5 deployment ID fixes. Notable changes also include the revamped context pruner with separate user/assistant budgets and the /connect Freebuff-only command registration.
ai.evidence: Diff hunk in freebuff/cli/release/package.json shows version changed from 0.0.20 to 0.0.21. Commit metadata categorizes this as a release-bump commit with category Packaging and areas Packaging.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.21 improves how you interact with AI models, especially for free-tier users, and makes the system smarter about managing conversation history and tracking usage. The context pruner now keeps more of your recent conversation intact by budgeting tokens separately for your messages and tool responses, so discussions stay relevant longer. Free mode gets stronger protections with rate limits (including a new 1 request per second cap) plus a country-detection fallback that reads location headers from your browser instead of relying solely on IP lookup. The system now records time-to-first-token (TTFT) on every response, giving better insight into model speed and performance, and Fireworks API requests carry session IDs for improved prompt caching. Upgrading gives you smoother, faster, and more reliable access to AI assistants, especially when using free credits, with fewer interruptions and clearer usage tracking throughout your session.

Engineers who rely on this test will see it evaluate against the same model that real users hit in production, so pass/fail results more closely mirror live behavior. ai.title: free-mode-rate-limiter test stability fixes
ai.summary: Refactored `free-mode-rate-limiter.test.ts` to remove reliance on `makeRequests` helper for per-second limit checks, replacing it with explicit loops. Updated time advancement logic in the 30-minute window test to advance by 1 minute instead of 1 second, ensuring the per-minute window expires before triggering the 30-minute limit. Scope limited to web API tests.

eli5.text: If you ever noticed the system that stops heavy usage from free accounts occasionally flagging people at the wrong time, that should stop happening now. The team rewrote the checks that verify how many requests you can make per second, and they also corrected the timing logic in the test that simulates a 30-minute usage window so it advances time correctly. This is behind-the-scenes maintenance limited to the automated tests for free-mode rate limiting, so there's no new behavior you'd see today, but the checks meant to enforce the 1 request per second limit on free-tier users are now more stable behind the scenes.

ai.title: CLI help banner shows workflow tip for connected ChatGPT OAuth
ai.summary: Help banner in cli/src/components/help-banner.tsx now displays a workflow tip (/interview → /plan → implement → /review) when ChatGPT OAuth is connected. Previously, only the connection prompt appeared for unconnected users. Scope limited to CLI help banner component.

eli5.text: When you ask the command-line tool for help, the friendly advice box at the top now changes based on whether you've connected your ChatGPT account. If you've already linked it, you'll see a quick workflow hint showing the recommended order of commands (/interview → /plan → implement → /review). If you haven't connected yet, nothing changes and you'll still just see the existing prompt to run /connect. This only affects the help screen shown right after launching the tool.

ai.title: setoutput accepts top-level or data-wrapped params
ai.summary: set_output handler now parses raw fields first, then falls back to `output.data` if top-level validation fails. This supports OpenAI strict schema enforcement by allowing a permissive `data: z.record(...)` input shape while injecting real outputSchema via prompt instructions. Agent prompt strings updated to explicitly mention both accepted formats. Validation errors now select the parse attempt with fewer Zod issues to provide more actionable retry feedback.

eli5.text: The set_output tool now accepts output fields either passed directly at the top level or wrapped inside a 'data' field, and when validation fails, it shows the error with fewer issues to help the agent retry more effectively. This is useful for AI agents that need flexibility in how they structure their outputs. Live today.

ai.title: Enable custom Fireworks deployment flag
ai.summary: Set `FIREWORKS_USE_CUSTOM_DEPLOYMENT` to `true` in `web/src/llm-api/fireworks.ts`. Switched active model in `scripts/test-fireworks-long.ts` to `accounts/james-65d217/deployments/lnfid5h9`. Scope covers Web API config and test scripts.

eli5.text: The system now uses a private, dedicated version of the AI model instead of the shared public one. If you were testing the connection to the AI service, you would notice requests going to a special endpoint owned by the development team rather than the default one. This only affects internal testing scripts and the part of the system that talks to the AI provider; regular users won't see any difference yet because the new setting hasn't been connected to live features.

ai.title: Add X close button to ChatGPT connect banner
ai.summary: Replaces the static `esc` hint with an interactive `x` close button in `cli/src/components/chatgpt-connect-banner.tsx`. The button calls `setInputMode('default')` from `useChatStore` to dismiss the banner. Applies to connected, error, loading, and initial states.

eli5.text: The ChatGPT connection banner now shows a clickable X button to close it, instead of telling you to press the Esc key. When you see the banner while connecting, authenticating, or if it errors out, you can click the X to dismiss it and return to your normal chat view. Hovering over the X highlights it, confirming it's interactive. This change is live today for anyone using the CLI.
